_what: The adjudicated contents of the three sign-off registers: for every board id that appears in a register's text, whether it is an ENTRY (the register is telling a named professional that this item waits on them) or a MENTION (the id appears in passing prose and gives the item no home).
_why: A loose scan for board ids cannot tell those two apart, and if it guesses ENTRY it hides exactly the failure the check exists to find - an item name-dropped in a note would look housed. Phase 113c checked every match by hand on 9 September 2026 and every one happened to be a genuine entry, so the loose scan was safe THAT DAY and is not safe as a design. This file is that judgement, written down once, so the check can be strict instead of generous.
_how_it_stays_honest: The check FAILS when a register's text contains a board id this file does not classify, and FAILS when this file names an id the register's text no longer contains. So it cannot quietly go stale: adding an entry to a register without recording it here is a red run, and so is deleting one.
_entry_shapes_in_use: Two, and the second exists because of a tooling limit recorded in COORDINATES: a row in the register's Appendix 3 index table, or a prose note declaring an entry. A row cannot be added to an existing Monday table through the document API, so every entry added after a register's table was built is declared in prose beside it. SV-S7, SV-S8, SDP-L3, SDP-V3, SDP-L4, SDP-L5, SDP-P5 to SDP-P8 and SDP-V4 are all of that second kind. Since 15 September 2026 (Phase 132d) every entry code in all three registers carries its register's prefix - SV- for FOR THE SURVEYOR, ACC- for FOR THE ACCOUNTANT, SDP- for FOR THE SOLICITOR, THE DPO AND THE DEVELOPER - in the registers themselves and in the refs here; the check matches board ids and counts, never a ref's code.
_boardIds: A board id looks exactly like an item id, and every register's Appendix 3 opens by naming the board. These are boards, and the check skips them rather than asking anybody to classify them as entries.
